Answer: C
Reason: The initial chest X-ray (Figure 1a) shows a massive, well-circumscribed opacity occupying the right hemithorax with smooth borders and no air bronchograms, which is characteristic of a large pleural-based soft tissue tumor like a liposarcoma rather than pneumonia, effusion, or embolism. The subsequent image (Figure 1c) showing post-surgical changes (clips) and lung re-expansion further supports the diagnosis of a resected mass.
